CAST: ORLA=f, BRAM=m, MR. PELL=m, MRS. PELL=f, ANNOUNCER=m, NARRATOR=m

[MUSIC: Theme opens, a slow organ line, then fades]

ANNOUNCER: THE LIGHTHOUSE SUPPER.
Episode 1: The Last Ferry.
We join the keepers of Gull Rock on the night the supply boat is due.

[MUSIC: Bridge, brighter]

[BED: Wind over rock, a distant bell buoy]

NARRATOR: October, 1931.
At the top of the stair, the lamp room glows.
The Pells have rowed out for the evening.

MR. PELL: (laughs) I tell you, Bram, the mainland is in a flap.
The harbour board wants every light inspected by Friday.

BRAM: Let them inspect.
We are far enough out to see them coming.

[SFX: Spoon against a tin cup]

MRS. PELL: It is a worry, really.
To think they might take the lamp from us.

ORLA: (dryly) They will need a longer ladder than the one they have.

BRAM: (boisterous) Which is why we are eating the good ham tonight!

[SFX: A chair scraping on stone]

MR. PELL: (reverberating) Hold the lamp steady!
It is swinging on its chain.

ORLA: (softly) It is only the wind, Mr. Pell.

BRAM: (stubbornly) Even if they come, we have the cellar and the tide tables.

[BED: off]

ORLA: (approaching) You are still at those ledgers.

BRAM: (smiling) Leave the lamp lit, Orla.

ORLA: (small laugh) You always did have an appetite.
And you always did pay for it in oil.

NARRATOR: (sighs) Outside, the bell buoy rang once and went quiet.
The keepers did not
hear the boat until morning.

[SFX: Oars, far off]

[MUSIC: Closing theme, organ, swelling and out]

ANNOUNCER: Next week, the inspector arrives.
